### Route directories (reader side)
```
src/routes/(course-reader)/
    course/[courseid]/         -- Course home page
    topic/[courseid]/[...loid]/ -- Topic pages
    lab/[courseid]/[...loid]/   -- Interactive labs
    talk/[courseid]/[...loid]/  -- Presentations (PDF or Marp)
    note/[courseid]/[...loid]/  -- Notes/documents
    notebook/[courseid]/[...loid]/ -- Jupyter notebooks
    video/[courseid]/[...loid]/ -- Videos
    wall/[type]/[courseid]/     -- Gallery walls
    tutorial/[courseid]/[...loid]/ -- Tutorials
    paneltalk/[courseid]/[...loid]/ -- Panel talks
    search/[courseid]/          -- Search
    time/[courseid]/            -- Analytics
    llm/[courseid]/             -- LLM view
```

### Source course folder naming (authoring convention)
From the test course JSON `id` fields, the convention is:
- **Topics**: `topic-NN-name` (e.g., `topic-01-mermaid`, `topic-02-marp`)
- **Units**: `unit-N` (e.g., `unit-1`)
- **Notes**: `note-N-name` (e.g., `note-1-flowchart`)
- **Talks**: `talk-N-name` (e.g., `talk-1-marp-intro`)
- **Labs**: typically `lab-NN` or `lab-N-name`
- **Sides**: `side` type -- supplementary content alongside units

The `{{COURSEURL}}` placeholder in route patterns (`D:\code\tutors\test-course\tutors.json`, line 2) is replaced at runtime with the actual course ID by `injectCourseUrl()` in `D:\code\tutors\src\lib\services\course\services\lo-tree.ts` (line 114).

## 5. Content Types and How They Are Rendered

### Markdown Content
All learning objects have `contentMd` (raw markdown) and `contentHtml` (rendered HTML). Markdown is processed by `markdown-it` with these plugins (from `D:\code\tutors\node_modules\@tutors\tutors-model-lib\src\utils\markdown-utils.ts`):
- LaTeX/KaTeX math
- Anchors and TOC
- Emoji, subscript, superscript, mark, footnotes, definition lists
- Video and podcast player embeds
- Shiki syntax highlighting for code blocks

### Marp Slides
Detected via `isMarpContent()` in `D:\code\tutors\src\lib\services\markdown\services\marp-renderer.ts` (line 3). A talk is Marp if:
- `lo.frontMatter.marp === true` or `"true"`, OR
- The `contentMd` starts with `---\nmarp: true`

Marp talks are rendered by `TalkMarp.svelte` (`D:\code\tutors\src\lib\ui\learning-objects\content\TalkMarp.svelte`) using a server-side API at `/api/marp`. The `TalkClient.svelte` (`D:\code\tutors\src\lib\ui\learning-objects\content\TalkClient.svelte`) dynamically switches between Marp, Mozilla PDF viewer, and Adobe PDF viewer based on the content type and course settings.

### Jupyter Notebooks
Type `"notebook"` with a Jupyter icon (`simple-icons:jupyter`). The notebook Lo has:
- `cells[]` array with `cellType: "markdown" | "code" | "raw"`
- `kernelLanguage` (defaults to `"python"`)
- Each cell has `source`, `outputs[]`, and `executionCount`

Rendered by `Notebook.svelte` (`D:\code\tutors\src\lib\ui\learning-objects\content\Notebook.svelte`) with a sidebar cell navigator, code highlighting via Shiki, and expandable code outputs. Notebook markdown is processed by `convertNotebookToHtml()` in `D:\code\tutors\src\lib\services\markdown\services\markdown.svelte.ts` (line 181).

### Labs
Multi-step interactive tutorials. A `Lab` has `los: LabStep[]` where each step has its own `contentMd`. The `LiveLab` class (`D:\code\tutors\src\lib\services\course\services\live-lab.ts`) manages step navigation, converting each step's markdown independently.

### Talks (PDF)
Standard talks use PDF files (referenced via `pdf` and `pdfFile` fields). Can be displayed through Adobe or Mozilla PDF viewers depending on the `defaultPdfReader` property.

### Notes
Simple markdown content. Converted on-demand (not during initial tree decoration) by `convertNoteToHtml()`.

## 6. Course Tree Decoration Pipeline

The data flow from JSON to rendered content (`D:\code\tutors\src\lib\services\course\services\lo-tree.ts`):

1. `tutors.json` is fetched from `{courseUrl}/tutors.json`
2. `decorateCourseTree()` sets `courseId`, `courseUrl`, `route` on the course
3. `flattenLos()` recursively collects all nested Los
4. `injectCourseUrl()` replaces `{{COURSEURL}}` placeholders in routes, images, videos, and PDFs
5. `removeUnknownLos()` filters out `type: "unknown"` entries
6. `decorateLoTree()` recursively processes each Lo:
   - Sets `parentCourse` reference
   - Loads icons from frontMatter
   - Builds breadcrumbs
   - Converts contentMd to HTML (except labs, notes, notebooks -- those are on-demand)
   - For composite Los: extracts `panels` and `units` sub-collections
7. Builds `loIndex` (Map of route -> Lo) and `topicIndex` (Map of route -> Topic)
8. `loadPropertyFlags()` extracts course-level configuration from properties
9. `createCompanions()` builds companion link bar (Slack, Zoom, etc.)
10. `createWalls()` creates wall collections for each content type
11. `initCalendar()` processes calendar data if present

## 7. External Course References

The README (`D:\code\tutors\README.md`) points to these key external repos for understanding course authoring:

- **Reference Course source**: https://github.com/tutors-sdk/tutors-reference-course
- **Generator tools**: https://github.com/tutors-sdk/tutors-apps
- **Reference Manual**: https://github.com/tutors-sdk/tutors-reference-manual
- **Live reference course**: https://tutors.dev/course/reference-course

The `properties.yaml` authoring format and folder structure conventions (topic folders, unit folders, lab step files, etc.) are defined in the generator side (`tutors-apps`), not in this reader repository. The reader only consumes the compiled `tutors.json` output.

## 5. Content Types and How They Are Rendered

### Markdown Content
All learning objects have `contentMd` (raw markdown) and `contentHtml` (rendered HTML). Markdown is processed by `markdown-it` with these plugins (from `D:\code\tutors\node_modules\@tutors\tutors-model-lib\src\utils\markdown-utils.ts`):
- LaTeX/KaTeX math
- Anchors and TOC
- Emoji, subscript, superscript, mark, footnotes, definition lists
- Video and podcast player embeds
- Shiki syntax highlighting for code blocks

### Marp Slides
Detected via `isMarpContent()` in `D:\code\tutors\src\lib\services\markdown\services\marp-renderer.ts` (line 3). A talk is Marp if:
- `lo.frontMatter.marp === true` or `"true"`, OR
- The `contentMd` starts with `---\nmarp: true`

Marp talks are rendered by `TalkMarp.svelte` (`D:\code\tutors\src\lib\ui\learning-objects\content\TalkMarp.svelte`) using a server-side API at `/api/marp`. The `TalkClient.svelte` (`D:\code\tutors\src\lib\ui\learning-objects\content\TalkClient.svelte`) dynamically switches between Marp, Mozilla PDF viewer, and Adobe PDF viewer based on the content type and course settings.

### Jupyter Notebooks
Type `"notebook"` with a Jupyter icon (`simple-icons:jupyter`). The notebook Lo has:
- `cells[]` array with `cellType: "markdown" | "code" | "raw"`
- `kernelLanguage` (defaults to `"python"`)
- Each cell has `source`, `outputs[]`, and `executionCount`

Rendered by `Notebook.svelte` (`D:\code\tutors\src\lib\ui\learning-objects\content\Notebook.svelte`) with a sidebar cell navigator, code highlighting via Shiki, and expandable code outputs. Notebook markdown is processed by `convertNotebookToHtml()` in `D:\code\tutors\src\lib\services\markdown\services\markdown.svelte.ts` (line 181).

### Labs
Multi-step interactive tutorials. A `Lab` has `los: LabStep[]` where each step has its own `contentMd`. The `LiveLab` class (`D:\code\tutors\src\lib\services\course\services\live-lab.ts`) manages step navigation, converting each step's markdown independently.

### Talks (PDF)
Standard talks use PDF files (referenced via `pdf` and `pdfFile` fields). Can be displayed through Adobe or Mozilla PDF viewers depending on the `defaultPdfReader` property.

### Notes
Simple markdown content. Converted on-demand (not during initial tree decoration) by `convertNoteToHtml()`.

## 6. Course Tree Decoration Pipeline

The data flow from JSON to rendered content (`D:\code\tutors\src\lib\services\course\services\lo-tree.ts`):

1. `tutors.json` is fetched from `{courseUrl}/tutors.json`
2. `decorateCourseTree()` sets `courseId`, `courseUrl`, `route` on the course
3. `flattenLos()` recursively collects all nested Los
4. `injectCourseUrl()` replaces `{{COURSEURL}}` placeholders in routes, images, videos, and PDFs
5. `removeUnknownLos()` filters out `type: "unknown"` entries
6. `decorateLoTree()` recursively processes each Lo:
   - Sets `parentCourse` reference
   - Loads icons from frontMatter
   - Builds breadcrumbs
   - Converts contentMd to HTML (except labs, notes, notebooks -- those are on-demand)
   - For composite Los: extracts `panels` and `units` sub-collections
7. Builds `loIndex` (Map of route -> Lo) and `topicIndex` (Map of route -> Topic)
8. `loadPropertyFlags()` extracts course-level configuration from properties
9. `createCompanions()` builds companion link bar (Slack, Zoom, etc.)
10. `createWalls()` creates wall collections for each content type
11. `initCalendar()` processes calendar data if present
